SEARCH

All Classes and Interfaces

Class
Description
Bishop
A bishop, which moves any number of squares diagonally.
Board
The 8 × 8 chess board, stored as a grid of pieces, plus a record of every piece that has been captured.
BoardEvaluator
Scores a position so the computer can compare moves.
BoardPanel
Draws the chessboard and turns mouse clicks into squares.
ChessApp
The entry point for console chess.
ChessFrame
The main window: the board, the side panel and the menus.
ChessGuiApp
Starts the graphical chess game.
ChessRules
The single source of truth for which moves are legal.
Command
The things a player can type at the move prompt besides a move.
ConsoleUI
The text interface: shows the board, reads moves from the keyboard, and prints the result of each move.
Difficulty
The computer's difficulty levels.
Game
Runs a game of chess: holds the board and both players, tracks whose turn it is and the move history, checks every move against the rules, and tells its listeners what happened.
GameController
Connects the Swing view to the game: the "controller" in Model-View-Controller.
GameListener
Something that wants to be told when the game changes: the GUI panels, the logger and so on.
GameLogger
Writes game events to the log: game start, each move, rejected moves and the result.
GameSettings
The choices made in the New Game dialog.
GameStatus
The state of the game from the point of view of the side about to move.
InputParser
Turns what the player types into a command or a move.
King
A king, which moves exactly one square in any direction.
Knight
A knight, which moves in an L shape: two squares in one direction and one square to the side.
LoggingMoveStrategy
Wraps another strategy and logs each move it chooses and how long it took.
LoggingSetup
Sets up Java's built-in logging (java.util.logging) to write one line per event to logs/chess.log.
LoggingSetup.OneLineFormatter
Formats a log record as 2026-12-02 14:05:31 INFO message.
MinimaxAI
The Medium and Hard levels: searches ahead with minimax and alpha-beta pruning.
Move
One chess move: which piece moved, where from and to, what it captured, and what kind of move it was.
MoveResult
The outcome of trying a move: whether it worked, and a message explaining what happened or why it was rejected.
MoveStrategy
A way of choosing a move for the computer.
MoveType
The kinds of moves in chess.
NewGameDialog
Lets the user choose a game type: against the computer (color and difficulty) or two players at one screen.
Pawn
A pawn, the only piece whose movement depends on its color.
Piece
The superclass for all six chess pieces.
PieceColor
The two players in a chess game.
PieceFactory
Creates pieces from their one-letter codes.
PieceGlyphs
Draws chess pieces with the Unicode chess symbols (U+2654 to U+265F), so no image files are needed.
Player
One of the two people playing, identified by a name and the color they play.
Position
A square on the chess board, stored as an array row and column.
PromotionDialog
Asks which piece a pawn should become, using a standard JOptionPane with one button per choice.
PromotionPiece
The four pieces a pawn can be promoted to when it reaches the far rank.
Queen
A queen, which moves any number of squares in a straight line or diagonally, combining the rook's and bishop's movement.
RandomAI
The Easy level: picks any legal move at random.
Rook
A rook, which moves any number of squares horizontally or vertically.
SafeMoveSelector
Wraps another strategy and checks its answer.
SidePanel
The panel beside the board: whose turn it is, status messages, captured pieces, the move list and the main buttons.
SidePanel.CapturedStrip
One row of captured pieces, drawn small.
SidePanel.Tone
Kinds of status message, each shown in its own color.
